# Tier-aware recipe-book CLI blocks — Intake Brief

**Work Item:** `TF-0MV4Z4O8I008IZZX` | **Type:** docs | **Priority:** Medium
**Blocks / Blocked-by:** Blocked-by `TF-0MV290BG8003GXXH`

> **Headline:** Make each recipe-book page's `## ToneForge CLI` block
> **tier-aware** so it demonstrates the pipeline stage appropriate to that tier,
> generated from a single shared builder driven by the roster `tier` (and the
> arrangement kind for capstones), with tests that keep every block fresh and
> valid.

## Problem statement

Every one of the 100 recipe pages currently carries the **same** four-command
`## ToneForge CLI` block (`generate` ×2, `show`, `list recipes`) regardless of
tier, so the book does not teach the ToneForge pipeline progressively. The
seven tiers were designed to illustrate distinct tooling stages
(`analyze`, `classify`/`explore`, `sequence`/`library`, `visualize`,
`stack`) but the pages do not surface them. The block text is also duplicated
in `generate-cli-blocks.ts` and `generate-pages.ts`, and is only checked for
marker *presence* — not freshness — so it cannot stay honest as tiers evolve.

## Users

- **Game developers** working the book front-to-back who learn the tooling in
  the same order as the recipes: each page should show the CLI surface that
  produced or evaluates that tier.
- **Sound designers / technical artists** who want the commands on a page to be
  runnable and to demonstrate the relevant stage (e.g. `classify` for a
  textured recipe, `stack` for a multi-voice sting).
- **ToneForge maintainers** who need the blocks to come from one source of truth
  and the test suite to fail when a page drifts from the generator.

Example user stories:

- As a developer reading Tier 3, I want the page to show `classify` and
  `explore`, so I can see how the tooling evaluates a textured sound.
- As a maintainer, I want one shared block builder, so I cannot introduce a
  third copy of the command text.
- As a maintainer, I want the tests to compare each page's block against the
  generator, so a stale block fails CI.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Tier-aware blocks.** Every one of the 100 recipe pages' `## ToneForge CLI`
  block contains the command surfaces required for its roster `tier`, per the
  mapping below, and **no** recipe page still carries the previous generic
  four-command block. Each block replaces the generic commands rather than
  appending to them.

  | Tier | Required command surfaces | Example commands (illustrative) |
  |------|---------------------------|----------------------------------|
  | 1 — Pure tones & blips | `generate`, `show`, `list recipes` | `toneforge generate --recipe <name> --seed 42 --output <name>.wav`; `toneforge show <name>`; `toneforge list recipes --tags casual` |
  | 2 — Shaped events | `generate`, `analyze` | `toneforge generate --recipe <name> --seed 42 --output <name>.wav`; `toneforge analyze --recipe <name> --seed 42` |
  | 3 — Textured & filtered | `classify`, `explore` | `toneforge classify --recipe <name> --seed 42`; `toneforge explore sweep --recipe <name> --seed-range 1:50 --keep-top 5` |
  | 4 — Melodic motifs | `sequence`, `library` | `toneforge sequence inspect --preset presets/sequences/casual_level_complete_sequence.json`; `toneforge library list` |
  | 5 — Character & critter voices | `classify`, `visualize` | `toneforge classify --recipe <name> --seed 42`; `toneforge visualize export --recipe <name> --seed 42 --format frames` |
  | 6 — Ambience & loops | `sequence`, `explore` | `toneforge sequence inspect --preset presets/sequences/footsteps_run.json`; `toneforge explore sweep --recipe <name> --seed-range 1:50 --keep-top 5` |
  | 7 — Multi-voice stings | `stack`, `visualize` | `toneforge stack inspect --preset presets/stacks/casual_victory_stack.json`; `toneforge visualize export --recipe <name> --seed 42 --format frames` |

- **Single shared builder + idempotence.** One shared block renderer, driven by
  the roster `tier` for recipe pages and by the arrangement kind for capstones,
  is the only source of block text used by `generate-cli-blocks.ts`,
  `generate-pages.ts` and `generate-capstones.ts`. Running the generators twice
  produces byte-identical `docs/recipe-book/*.md` (idempotent regeneration).

- **Valid commands and references.** Every command in a block uses a current,
  valid ToneForge subcommand/flag; every `--recipe <name>` resolves to the
  page's recipe (or another registered recipe); and every `--preset <path>`
  resolves to an existing file under `presets/`. Capstone `## ToneForge CLI`
  blocks are wrapped in machine-readable
  `<!-- CLI_BLOCK_START … -->`/`<!-- CLI_BLOCK_END -->` markers.

- **Tests enforce freshness (testing/validation).**
  `src/recipes/recipe-book.test.ts` validates each recipe page's block by
  comparing it to the shared builder output (not marker presence), asserts each
  tier's block contains exactly its required surfaces, asserts capstone block
  markers exist and are fresh, and asserts every `--preset` reference exists.
  A drifted committed page fails the suite.

- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Fix the generators, not the pages.** Change `scripts/recipe-book/*.ts` and
  regenerate `docs/recipe-book/*`; hand-editing generated pages is out of scope.
- **Single source of truth.** Do not add a second/third copy of block text;
  reuse (or create) the shared builder. Build on the shared builder, corrected
  `toneforge show <name>` positional command, capstone markers and freshness
  test delivered by `TF-0MV290BG8003GXXH` rather than duplicating them.
- **Sequenced after the parent.** This item is **blocked-by**
  `TF-0MV290BG8003GXXH` (same generator files, overlapping capstone-marker
  scope) and does not block it.
- **No change to recipe content or architecture.** Recipe YAML, roster,
  registry, parameter tables and sound-design narratives are untouched.
- **Preserve book conventions** — front matter (`title`/`id`/`order`/
  `description`), roster order, tier structure and all existing green gates.
- **UK English** throughout.
- `sequence`/`stack` commands require `--preset` (no `--recipe`), so T4/T6/T7
  reference a fixed, existing representative preset; pick one that is topically
  representative and keep the reference stable.

## Existing state

- `scripts/recipe-book/generate-cli-blocks.ts` — standalone generate/validate
  script; emits the fixed four commands.
- `scripts/recipe-book/generate-pages.ts` — `generateCliBlock(name)` duplicate
  used when rendering the 100 recipe pages.
- `scripts/recipe-book/generate-capstones.ts` — already emits **kind-aware**
  stack/sequence commands (`stack inspect|render`, `sequence inspect|generate`,
  `list stacks|sequences`) but with **no** CLI-block markers.
- `src/recipes/recipe-book.test.ts` — `expectCliBlockFresh()` only asserts that
  `<!-- CLI_BLOCK_START` / `<!-- CLI_BLOCK_END -->` exist on recipe pages.
- The per-tier tooling intent is already documented in the seven tier work
  items' ACs (epic `TF-0MUY9H7QZ000UX5W`).

## Desired change

- Extract a pure shared builder (e.g. `scripts/recipe-book/cli-blocks.ts`) that
  maps a recipe's `tier` to its command list and renders the marker-wrapped
  block, and make `generate-cli-blocks.ts`, `generate-pages.ts` and
  `generate-capstones.ts` all use it.
- Make the recipe-page block tier-aware per the mapping above; keep capstone
  blocks arrangement-kind-aware and wrap them in markers.
- Regenerate every recipe and capstone page.
- Strengthen `src/recipes/recipe-book.test.ts` with real freshness, per-tier
  surface, capstone-marker and preset-existence assertions.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/recipe-book/generate-cli-blocks.ts` — host (or delegate to) the
  tier→surface mapping and shared renderer; keep the `--validate` path.
- `scripts/recipe-book/generate-pages.ts` — remove the duplicated
  `generateCliBlock()`; call the shared tier-aware builder.
- `scripts/recipe-book/generate-capstones.ts` — render capstone blocks via the
  shared builder; wrap in markers; validate freshness.
- `scripts/recipe-book/cli-blocks.ts` (new, if the parent has not already
  introduced a shared module) — pure, side-effect-free `renderCliBlock(name,
  tier)` / kind-aware renderer importable by scripts **and** tests.
- `docs/recipe-book/*.md` — regenerated output (100 recipe pages + 10 capstone
  pages).
- `src/recipes/recipe-book.test.ts` — tier-aware freshness/surface/preset tests.
- `docs/recipe-book/index.md`, `README.md` — only if the tier→tooling mapping
  needs documenting for readers.

## Related work (manual)

- `Tier-aware recipe-book CLI blocks (progressive tooling per tier) (TF-0MV4Z4O8I008IZZX)` — this item, deferred out of the parent review.
- `Review the 100 sound library documentation (TF-0MV290BG8003GXXH)` — **blocking** parent: fixes the `show` command, adds the shared builder, capstone markers and freshness test.
- `Casual Game Recipe Book: 100 Documented Recipes from Simple to Stings (TF-0MUY9H7QZ000UX5W)` — completed epic that produced the book.
- Tier 1–7 work items (`TF-0MUYBDMHM003TI3D`, `TF-0MUYBDMUK0017P9H`, `TF-0MUYBDN7U002PDCQ`, `TF-0MUYBDNKI001IHW4`, `TF-0MUYBDNXI003BNUF`, `TF-0MUYBDOAE006OK3D`, `TF-0MUYBDONM008UGQW`) — source of the per-tier tooling mapping.
- `Capstone Arrangements (TF-0MUYBDP0L001QIVX)` — capstone stack/sequence presets and pages.
- `Fix recipe-book gate vacuity and index ordering (TF-0MUYJT9PP004JMV7)` — precedents for strengthening recipe-book tests.
- `scripts/recipe-book/generate-cli-blocks.ts`, `scripts/recipe-book/generate-pages.ts`, `scripts/recipe-book/generate-capstones.ts`, `src/recipes/recipe-book.test.ts` — the files to change.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **TF-0MM79EVKX0TSVWQC** – Collection & Economy Recipes (Tier 3) (completed)
- **TF-0MV29HYZU001WUW7** – Sound Module Index — catalogue all modules by primary function (completed)
- **TF-0MM0BWFC515OBCEO** – CLI UX & Commands (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `standups/2026_10_05.md` — matched: add, analyze, appropriate, around, aware (+44 more)
- `docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md` — matched: add, analyze, appropriate, around, aware (+38 more)
- `README.md` — matched: add, analyze, aware, block, book (+32 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: command drift.** A documented example command may stop matching the
  CLI. *Mitigation:* assert valid surfaces and that every referenced
  `--preset`/`--recipe` target exists; run a smoke check during implementation.
- **Risk: brittle tests.** Exact-line equality across 110 pages could make
  future recipe edits noisy. *Mitigation:* the freshness test compares against
  the shared builder (single source of truth), while tier assertions check
  command *surfaces* rather than full lines.
- **Risk: duplicated capstone-marker work.** The parent already adds capstone
  markers. *Mitigation:* this item is blocked-by the parent and extends marker
  coverage to freshness validation rather than re-adding markers.
- **Risk: scope creep** (richer per-page narrative, more tier-specific flags).
  *Mitigation:* record further ideas as `discovered-from:TF-0MV4Z4O8I008IZZX`
  items, not in this scope.
- **Assumption:** `TF-0MV290BG8003GXXH` lands first, providing the shared
  builder, the positional `toneforge show <name>` command, capstone markers and
  the freshness test this item builds on.
- **Assumption:** T4/T6/T7 use fixed representative presets
  (`casual_level_complete_sequence.json`, `footsteps_run.json`,
  `casual_victory_stack.json`) because `sequence`/`stack` require `--preset`;
  the implementer may substitute a topically closer existing preset.
- **Assumption:** freshness is validated by importing a pure shared builder in
  the test (no side-effecting generator subprocess).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Round 1 (producer, interactive reply) confirmed the per-tier command mapping,
block composition and sequencing against the parent item.

- **Q1 (round 1 — exact commands for T4/T6/T7).** The tier ACs name only
  "`sequence` (light) and `library`" (T4), "`sequence` and `explore`" (T6) and
  "`stack` concepts and `visualize`" (T7); these recipes are neither sequences
  nor stacks, so the exact commands were ambiguous. Options: A. concrete
  commands on the recipe where supported, otherwise a representative preset;
  B. always the specific capstone that uses the recipe (recipe→capstone
  lookup); C. one command per tier; D. freeform.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply): A.** Use concrete commands on the
    recipe where the surface supports `--recipe` (`classify`, `explore`,
    `visualize`, `analyze`), and a fixed representative `--preset` for the
    `sequence`/`stack` surfaces. Evidence: tier work items' ACs; CLI option
    inspection (`sequence`/`stack` accept only `--preset`).
- **Q2 (round 1 — block composition).** A. replace the generic four commands
  entirely; B. keep a `generate`+`show` baseline then append; C. replace but
  keep `generate`.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply): A.** Replace entirely, matching the
    item's stated intent ("instead of repeating the same four commands"); the
    central discovery workflow is covered by the index's *Working with the CLI*
    section.
- **Q3 (round 1 — sequencing vs the parent).** Should this item be
  blocked-by `TF-0MV290BG8003GXXH`, which edits the same generators and already
  adds capstone markers? A. yes; B. keep independent.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply): A.** Record `Blocked-by:
    TF-0MV290BG8003GXXH` to serialise overlapping generator edits. Evidence:
    parent's Key Files and desired change.

# Tier-aware CLI-block test coverage — test-first

**Parent:** `TF-0MV4Z4O8I008IZZX` | **Type:** task (test-first) | **Priority:** Medium

> **Goal:** Give the recipe book a failing-first test battery that pins the
> per-tier CLI-block contract *before* the shared builder is made tier-aware, so
> the builder cannot silently regress to the generic four-command block.

## Context

The blocking parent `TF-0MV290BG8003GXXH` already delivered:

- `buildCliBlock(name)` as the single source of truth in
  `scripts/recipe-book/generate-cli-blocks.ts`;
- marker-wrapped recipe blocks and marker-wrapped capstone blocks;
- byte-for-byte freshness assertions (`expectCliBlockFresh`,
  `expectCapstoneCliBlockFresh`) in `src/recipes/recipe-book.test.ts`.

What is missing is coverage of *what* each tier's block contains (the
progressive tooling surfaces) and that referenced preset paths resolve.

## Required test coverage

1. **Per-tier surface matrix.** For each tier 1–7, assert the shared tier-aware
   builder's output contains that tier's required command surfaces (and no
   others):

   | Tier | Required command surfaces |
   |------|---------------------------|
   | 1 — Pure tones & blips | `generate`, `show`, `list recipes` |
   | 2 — Shaped events | `generate`, `analyze` |
   | 3 — Textured & filtered | `classify`, `explore` |
   | 4 — Melodic motifs | `sequence`, `library` |
   | 5 — Character & critter voices | `classify`, `visualize` |
   | 6 — Ambience & loops | `sequence`, `explore` |
   | 7 — Multi-voice stings | `stack`, `visualize` |

2. **No generic block remains.** Assert no recipe page's CLI block still
   carries the previous generic command set (the default-seed `generate` line
   and the `list recipes --tags casual` line) except where the tier mapping
   legitimately requires the surface (Tier 1 keeps `list recipes`).

3. **Preset references resolve.** Every `--preset <path>` in a recipe or
   capstone CLI block points to an existing file under `presets/`.

4. **Freshness retained.** The existing byte-for-byte freshness assertions
   (page block == shared builder output; capstone block == shared builder
   output) must continue to hold; no marker-presence-only checks.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `src/recipes/recipe-book.test.ts` asserts, for every tier 1–7, that the
  shared builder's block contains exactly that tier's required command
  surfaces.
- [ ] A test fails if any recipe page still carries the previous generic
  four-command block.
- [ ] A test asserts every `--preset` reference in recipe and capstone CLI
  blocks resolves to an existing file under `presets/`.
- [ ] Tests enforce freshness (testing/validation): the existing byte-for-byte
  assertions remain and compare page and capstone blocks against the shared
  builder output, not marker presence alone.
- [ ] Written test-first: the new assertions fail against the current fixed
  four-command builder and pass once the tier-aware builder lands.

**Key Files:**

- `src/recipes/recipe-book.test.ts` — add the tier-surface matrix,
  generic-block and preset-existence tests; keep the freshness assertions.

**Notes:**
- The exact exported builder name (e.g. `buildRecipeCliBlock(name, tier)`) is
  agreed with the sibling implementation child *Tier-aware shared CLI-block
  builder and generator wiring* (a direct dependency) — keep the interface
  minimal.
- This is a test/verification task and deliberately precedes its
  implementation sibling (test-first ordering).

# Leaf of Completion — Intake Brief

**Work Item:** TF-0MV9OLWO6005ZI8E | **Type:** feature | **Priority:** medium

> **Headline:** Create a leitmotif for wave/level completion that conveys relief
> at finishing a stage coupled with worry about what's next — delivered as a
> ToneGraph recipe, two sequence presets (wave + level variants), recipe-book
> documentation, and full harness tests, all in the existing casual/arcade family.

## Problem statement

All existing end-of-stage sounds in the ToneForge recipe book (e.g.
`casual_level_complete_sequence`, `motif-quest-complete`, `sting-level-complete`)
convey pure celebration — an upward, resolved, major-tonality fanfare. A
leitmotif for **wave/level completion** should capture a more nuanced emotional
arc: **relief** at clearing a stage, followed by a subtle **worry** about the
next one. ToneForge currently has no asset in this emotional space.

## Users

- **Game developers** building wave-based casual/arcade games (tower defence,
  endless runners, bullet-hell-lite) who need a reusable, tonal-leader sound
  that plays at both wave-end and level-end without sounding identical.
- **Sound designers** and technical artists learning ToneForge who want a
  recipe-book example of leitmotif variation (same theme, two variants).

Example user stories:

- As a game developer, I want a wave-complete leitmotif that starts with relief
  (resolved, bright) and tails into a subtle worry (unresolved interval), so
  players feel the emotional arc of "almost done… but there's more."
- As a sound designer, I want a level-end variant of that leitmotif that feels
  bigger and more final, so I can reuse the core theme with one additional
  voice or longer decay.
- As a ToneForge user, I want the leitmotif to live in the casual/arcade family
  so it layers cleanly with existing recipes (blips, jingles, stings).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **`motif-waves-end` recipe** exists as `presets/recipes/motif-waves-end.yaml`,
   validates against the ToneGraph schema, and renders a ~1.2–1.6 s sound in
   the casual/arcade family: a short resolved phrase (relief) followed by a
   raised-4th or tritone tail (worry).
2. **`sequence-wave-end`** exists as `presets/sequences/sequence-wave-end.json`,
   plays `motif-waves-end` as a single compact event (~1.5 s).
3. **`sequence-level-end`** exists as `presets/sequences/sequence-level-end.json`,
   plays `motif-waves-end` with a second voice layered (e.g. `sting-level-complete`
   or a harmony line) at the resolution point for a bigger, more final feel.
4. **`docs/recipe-book/motif-waves-end.md`** — Sound design section (leitmotif
   explanation, note sequence, emotional arc, seed behaviour) + CLI block.
5. **`docs/recipe-book/sequence-wave-end.md`** and
   **`docs/recipe-book/sequence-level-end.md`** — both with Sound design + CLI
   blocks describing the sequence arrangement.
6. **Harness battery passes**: schema validation, determinism (fixed seed →
   identical output across runs), non-silence, index entry.
7. **Tags**: `casual`, `joy`, `fun`, `leitmotif`, `wave-complete`, `level-complete`.
8. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes — new recipe-book pages, regenerated `docs/recipe-book/index.md`, and any affected code comments.
9. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes (unit + smoke; no CI/CD pipeline tests).

## Constraints

- Must follow the existing ToneGraph `version: '0.1'` schema and use the same
  node types already present in the recipe book (oscillator, fmPattern, gain,
  envelope, destination).
- Must be **casual/arcade**: bright tonal centre (C major, default 392 Hz),
  short duration (total sequence < 3 s), no sustained drones or orchestral
  textures.
- Deterministic: same seed → byte-identical output (inherited ToneForge property).
- No new TypeScript dependencies or core changes required — file-backed YAML
  recipes only.

## Existing state

- **Relief-only sounds**: `motif-quest-complete` (Tier 4), `jingle-level-up`,
  `sting-level-complete`, `casual_level_complete_sequence` — all upward/major
  celebration with no unresolved tension.
- **Leitmotif pattern**: `gameover_melody.json` demonstrates the sequence
  pattern (same event at different seeds/times), but in a descending, sad
  contour — not relevant to the relief+worry emotional space.
- **Sequence infrastructure**: `presets/sequences/*.json` (29 entries),
  `scripts/recipe-book/generate-pages.ts` and `generate-cli-blocks.ts` for
  docs generation, `roster.ts` for the 100-item canonical manifest.
- **Harvested stings**: `sting-level-complete` (Tier 7, FM + harmony) could be
  used as the layer for the level-end variant.

## Desired change

A new leitmotif family under the `motif-` prefix:

```
motif-waves-end          — core recipe (relief → worry)
sequence-wave-end.json   — compact single-event sequence
sequence-level-end.json  — expanded two-voice sequence
docs/recipe-book/motif-waves-end.md
docs/recipe-book/sequence-wave-end.md
docs/recipe-book/sequence-level-end.md
```

All integrated into the Casual Game Recipe Book (TF-0MUY9H7QZ000UX5W) with
regenerated index and tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `presets/recipes/motif-waves-end.yaml` — Core leitmotif recipe (new).
- `presets/sequences/sequence-wave-end.json` — Wave-end sequence (new).
- `presets/sequences/sequence-level-end.json` — Level-end sequence (new).
- `docs/recipe-book/motif-waves-end.md` — Sound design narrative (new).
- `docs/recipe-book/sequence-wave-end.md` — Sequence narrative (new).
- `docs/recipe-book/sequence-level-end.md` — Sequence narrative (new).
- `src/recipes/recipe-book/roster.ts` — roster entry for the motif recipe (modified; see Open Question re the 100-entry invariant).
- `scripts/recipe-book/generate-capstones.ts` — CAPSTONES + CAPSTONE_USES entries for the two new sequences (modified). Note: `generate-pages.ts` covers recipes only; sequence pages are capstone-generated.
- `scripts/recipe-book/generate-index.ts` — capstones list and "Ten capstone arrangements" prose (modified).
- `src/recipes/recipe-book.test.ts` and `src/recipes/recipe-book-capstones.test.ts` — capstone arrays and page-count baselines (modified; required for the suite to pass).
- `docs/recipe-book/index.md` — regenerated with new entries (regenerated).
- `test/` — determinism/non-silence harness (existing, no changes if harness is generic).

## Related work

- **TF-0MUY9H7QZ000UX5W** — Casual Game Recipe Book: 100 Documented Recipes from
  Simple to Stings (parent epic, completed). This item feeds into that body.
- **TF-0MUYBDNKI001IHW4** — Tier 4: Melodic Motifs — establishes motif conventions
  (2–4 note figures, `motif-` prefix).
- **TF-0MUYBDONM008UGQW** — Tier 7: Multi-voice Stings — provides the `sting-*`
  family for level-end layering.
- **TF-0MM79FR9S17IZSP2** — Combo & Chain Recipes (Tier 6) — sequences demonstrate
  how multi-event compositions are assembled.

## Acceptance Criteria (final summary)

- **Testing/validation:** `motif-waves-end` passes the harness battery — schema validation, determinism (same seed → byte-identical output across runs), non-silence, and index presence; both sequences render without error.
- **Documentation:** all related documentation updated (recipe-book pages, index, code comments).
- **Suite:** full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Risks & Assumptions

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| "Relief + worry" emotional arc is hard to achieve in a < 2 s sound | AC quality | Default to clear resolution (perfect 5th) + subtle raised 4th tail; test at multiple seeds |
| Sequence docs not generated by existing tooling (sequences lack narrative map) | Incomplete docs | Add sequence entries to narrative map in `generate-pages.ts`; small change |
| New items increase recipe book size beyond the original 100 | Scope creep | Treat as an extension (1 recipe + 2 sequences = 3 items); note in index |

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What deliverable format?" — Answer: **A** — Recipes + sequences + docs pages + tests. Source: producer reply.
- Q: "Wave vs level — one motif with two variants, two distinct motifs, or one shared?" — Answer: **A** — One leitmotif, two variants (wave = compact, level = bigger with extra voice). Source: producer reply.
- Q: "What musical character/genre — casual/arcade, fantasy, sci-fi, or open?" — Answer: **A** — Casual/arcade, bright C-major tonal centre, relief = upward resolved phrase, worry = raised 4th/♭5 tail interval. Source: producer reply.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **TF-0MUYBDNKI001IHW4** – Tier 4 -- Melodic Motifs (completed)
- **TF-0MV5KHE5A0000FKA** – Tier-aware shared CLI-block builder and generator wiring (blocked)
- **TF-0MUYBDM4X005O4N8** – Recipe Book Harness & Tracer Slice (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `standups/2026_10_05.md` — matched: 5th, add, additional, already, arc (+169 more)
- `docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md` — matched: acceptance, add, already, arc, asset (+146 more)
- `README.md` — matched: add, already, arc, asset, backed (+118 more)

# Playable MIDI instruments (Note On / Note Off) — Intake Brief

**Work Item:** TF-0MV9PIBNV008C00R | **Type:** epic | **Priority:** Medium

> **Headline:** A new `instruments` capability: purpose-crafted, polyphonic
> instruments defined as ToneGraph-shaped presets (oscillator + ADSR envelope
> + optional filter), driven live by a structured Note On / Note Off message
> API (`instrument.noteOn(note, velocity)` / `instrument.noteOff(note)`) on a
> deterministic, sample-accurate voice engine that runs in both the browser
> (Web Audio) and Node (`node-web-audio-api`).

## Problem statement

ToneForge plays fixed, one-shot sound events; there is no way to *play a
pitch* — to hold a voice while a key is down, change pitch per note, and
release it when the key lifts. MIDI Note On / Note Off is the natural way to
express that, and today nothing in the codebase maps a MIDI note number to a
live, sustained, re-triggerable sound. This item adds a family of playable
instruments plus the engine to drive them from a simple programmatic
Note On / Note Off API, so interactive and melodic use cases (game music,
prototyping, sound-design auditioning) no longer need to pre-render every
pitch.

## Users

- **Game developers / composers** prototyping interactive music or melodic
  SFX who want to trigger pitched voices expressively (note + velocity, held
  and released) without a DAW.
- **Sound designers** auditioning a ToneGraph patch across the full pitch
  range and different velocities before committing it to a library entry.
- **ToneForge maintainers** who need instruments to follow the same
  deterministic, seeded, tested conventions as the rest of the platform.

Example user stories:

- As a developer, I want `instrument.noteOn(60, 100)` then
  `instrument.noteOff(60)` to produce a sustained tone that starts on note 60
  (middle C), stays audible until the note-off, then releases — so I can play
  chords and melodies from game logic.
- As a composer, I want to hold multiple notes at once (e.g. a 3-note chord)
  and have the engine respect a voice limit with sensible stealing, so my
  usage stays predictable and CPU-safe.
- As a sound designer, I want each instrument preset to declare its own
  attack/decay/sustain/release so plucks behave differently from pads, and I
  want velocity to change loudness naturally.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Instrument note API:** each instrument exposes `noteOn(midiNote,
  velocity)` and `noteOff(midiNote)` backed by structured `midiNoteOn` /
  `midiNoteOff` message types; the engine maps MIDI notes to frequencies via
  the A4 (note 69) = 440 Hz equal-tempered formula (assertable: note 60 →
  261.63 Hz, note 69 → 440 Hz) and maps velocity (1–127) to gain.
- **ADSR envelope:** each instrument's envelope has attack / decay / sustain /
  release stages; Note On runs attack→decay→sustain-hold, Note Off runs
  release; an offline-render test asserts a held note produces non-silent
  audio during sustain and decays to silence after release.
- **Polyphony + voice management:** the engine is polyphonic with a
  configurable maximum-voice limit and a documented voice-stealing policy at
  the limit; re-triggering a note already sounding steals/replaces that
  note's own voice; tests cover chords at/over the limit and same-note
  retrigger.
- **Instrument family:** at least five instrument presets (e.g. pluck, pad,
  bass, bell, string-like lead) are defined, schema-valid, registered and
  discoverable, and each renders deterministic, non-silent audio for a given
  seed (offline render snapshot test).
- **Dual runtime:** rendering works in Node (real-time via
  `node-web-audio-api` and offline via `OfflineAudioContext`) and in the
  browser (real-time Web Audio; the existing web bundle builds without
  Node-specific imports).
- **Determinism:** same seed + same note/velocity sequence ⇒ identical output
  (byte-identical offline WAV), consistent with the platform's
  determinism guarantees.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Scope stays at the programmatic API** (decision Q1 = A): no raw MIDI byte
  decoder, no Web MIDI API hardware binding, and no MIDI file playback in this
  item — those are follow-ups.
- **New instrument definitions only** (decision Q2 = A): do not retrofit a
  recipe-as-instrument wrapper in this item; hand-crafted instrument presets
  first.
- Instruments must follow platform conventions: deterministic given seed,
  ToneGraph-shaped YAML/TS definitions, schema-validated, unit- and
  integration-tested, UK English.
- No changes to existing recipe/stack/sequence/CLI behaviour unless required
  for registration/discovery.
- Voice limits and stealing must be implemented in an injectable, unit-testable
  engine (like the mixer's voice tracking), not baked into the audio path.

## Existing state

- No MIDI or instrument support anywhere; `STACK_PRD.md` lists "MIDI
  sequencing" as a non-goal of the stack module.
- `src/sequence/` schedules SFX events over time (not pitched, held voices);
  `src/runtime/` loops whole rendered events with iteration-granular parameter
  changes — neither handles sample-accurate per-note voices.
- ToneGraph rendering (`src/core/tonegraph*.ts`, `src/core/renderer.ts`) and
  recipe YAML presets (`presets/recipes/*.yaml`) generate one-shot, mostly
  fixed-pitch audio; 77 of 100+ recipes already use oscillators.
- `src/audio/web-audio.ts` abstracts Web Audio for Node (`node-web-audio-api`
  installed) and browser; `web/src/audio.ts` already creates a real-time
  `AudioContext` in the browser.
- `src/mixer/runtime.ts` already tracks active voices per group
  (`maxVoices` / `activeVoices`) — a precedent for voice-limit policy.

## Desired change

- Add an `src/instruments/` module: instrument schema + validation, a
  `noteOn`/`noteOff` API with `midiNoteOn`/`midiNoteOff` message types and
  note→Hz / velocity→gain mapping, an ADSR envelope engine, a voice manager
  (polyphony, limit, stealing, same-note retrigger), and a deterministic
  renderer wired to both Node and browser Web Audio.
- Ship a starter family of 5+ instrument presets (pluck, pad, bass, bell,
  string-like lead), schema-validated and discoverable alongside the recipe
  library.
- Expose testing hooks (injectable clock, context, seed) so all behaviour is
  unit-testable; add offline-render snapshot tests for pitch, sustain,
  release, polyphony and determinism.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/instruments/schema.ts` — instrument definition schema (oscillator +
  ADSR + optional filter) and validation.
- `src/instruments/instrument.ts` — `Instrument` interface, `noteOn` /
  `noteOff`, `midiNoteOn` / `midiNoteOff` message types, note→Hz and
  velocity→gain mapping.
- `src/instruments/envelope.ts` — ADSR stage state machine (attack/decay/
  sustain/release).
- `src/instruments/voice-manager.ts` — polyphonic voice allocation, limit,
  stealing, same-note retrigger.
- `src/instruments/engine.ts` — deterministic voice renderer for Node
  (real-time + offline) and browser (real-time).
- `src/instruments/index.ts` — public exports and instrument registry.
- `src/instruments/presets/*` (or `presets/instruments/*.yaml`) — the starter
  instrument family (pluck, pad, bass, bell, string-like lead).
- `src/instruments/*.test.ts` — unit tests (mapping, envelope, polyphony,
  determinism) mirroring `src/recipes/*.test.ts` conventions.
- `docs/modules/instruments.md` (or equivalent module-index entry) — module
  documentation; README entry.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: real-time Web Audio in headless/CI environments.** *Mitigation:*
  inject `AudioContext`/`OfflineAudioContext`; tests use offline rendering
  unless a real-time context is explicitly required.
- **Risk: ambiguous voice-stealing policy** leads to surprising behaviour.
  *Mitigation:* document and unit-test the policy (e.g. steal the oldest
  sounding voice first; same-note retrigger replaces its own voice);
  configurability where reasonable.
- **Risk: scope creep** towards DAW-like features (pitch bend, CC,
  aftertouch, Web MIDI hardware, MIDI files, velocity curves, more
  instruments). *Mitigation:* recorded as explicit follow-up items, not this
  scope.
- **Risk: determinism drift from sample-rate/exception paths.** *Mitigation:*
  fixed 44100 Hz for snapshots; assert byte-identical offline output; reuse
  platform seed conventions.
- **Risk: browser/Node import split** (Node-only `node-web-audio-api` imports
  leaking into the web bundle). *Mitigation:* keep Web Audio access behind
  `src/audio/web-audio.ts`, matching the existing pattern and bundle tests.
- **Assumption:** note velocity maps monotonically to gain (linear or
  per-instrument curve) — exact curve decided in implementation with tests.
- **Assumption:** a starter family of five instruments plus the engine is the
  right first slice; the family can grow via follow-up items.

## Related work (manual)

- `Tier 4 -- Melodic Motifs (TF-0MUYBDNKI001IHW4)` — precedent for pitched
  oscillator recipes, but fixed-pitch one-shots; informs instrument preset
  craft.
- `Tier 7 -- Multi-voice Stings (TF-0MUYBDONM008UGQW)` — multi-voice
  precedent.
- `Runtime Features (TF-0MM4OWRQ70IWEKZ2)` and `Runtime session: continuous
  footsteps transport (TF-0MUYF87JH0089VQO)` — the start/stop continuous
  transport is the closest existing analog to Note On/Note Off sustain.
- `Mixer voice limiting tests (TF-0MMLC8SQ302DVYOZ)` — voice-limit precedent
  for the voice manager.
- `Web-Based Single-Sound Editor (TF-0MUTZ4TOY003DJ45)` — browser Web Audio
  real-time playback precedent.
- `docs/prd/SEQUENCER_PRD.md` — explicit boundary: the sequencer stays an
  SFX event scheduler; instruments are a distinct, complementary capability.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (playback surface / MIDI interpretation).** What should "played by
  sending MIDI Note On / Note Off" mean at the interface level?
  (A) programmatic Note On/Off API + structured message types driving real-time
  browser and Node; (B) A + raw MIDI byte decoder; (C) A/B + Web MIDI API
  hardware binding; (D) A/B + offline MIDI file playback.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **A — programmatic API only**.
    No byte decoder, hardware binding or MIDI-file playback in this item
    (recorded as follow-ups).
- **Q2 (instrument set / definition).** Where do the instruments come from?
  (A) new ToneGraph-shaped instrument definitions (oscillator + ADSR +
  optional filter) shipped as a preset family; (B) wrap existing recipes as
  instruments; (C) hybrid.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **A — new instrument
    definitions**, a purpose-crafted preset family first.
- **Q3 (polyphony / envelope semantics).** (A) polyphonic with configurable
  voice limit + stealing, per-note ADSR, Note Off → release, retrigger
  replaces the same note's voice; (B) monophonic; (C) polyphonic unlimited.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **A — polyphonic with a
    configurable voice limit and stealing, per-note ADSR, retrigger stealing
    the same note's voice.**

## Related work (automated report)

## Plan: decomposition (2026-10-15)

# Instrument test harness and offline fixtures

**Parent:** TF-0MV9PIBNV008C00R (Playable MIDI instruments)
**Type:** task (test infrastructure)

## Goal

Provide the shared, deterministic test utilities every instrument feature
depends on, so notes, envelopes, polyphony and presets can be asserted
reproducibly without ad-hoc test code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A reusable harness (e.g. `src/instruments/__tests__/helpers.ts`) renders a
  note/velocity sequence offline at a **pinned 44100 Hz** sample rate and
  returns the rendered `Float32Array` samples.
- The harness exposes analysis helpers used by later features: RMS / peak
  amplitude, silence detection, and dominant-frequency estimation (zero-crossing
  or DFT peak, within a documented tolerance).
- A smoke test proves the harness itself is deterministic (two identical runs
  produce identical output) and that analysis helpers behave correctly on
  synthetic tones (e.g. a generated 440 Hz sine reports ~440 Hz, a quiet buffer
  is reported silent).
- No production behaviour is introduced by this item; changes are limited to
  test utilities and fixtures.
- Naming, file layout and conventions mirror the existing shared helper
  precedent (e.g. the recipe test helper `src/recipes/__tests__/helpers.ts`).

**Key Files:**

- `src/instruments/__tests__/helpers.ts` (new)
- `src/instruments/__tests__/harness.test.ts` (new)

## Notes

Depends on nothing; enables all subsequent instrument features.
